description: deixis mandatory Node[T] construction vectors — which spellings construct a node. Every node has exactly one supplied T (ADR 0010 §1, §3), and keys are unique among siblings (§3). op "construct" takes a node spelling; its result is {"defined": <node>} when the spelling constructs, or {"undefined": {}} when it must not. A duplicate-key refusal is spelled as invalid.json spells it, {"error": "duplicate_key", "key": <hex>} at case level, so that it is specific. A missing value has no error class, because neither the spec nor the old corpus names one. A harness must never count a protocol error or an unsupported operation as a refusal (MNODE-PLAN). Every case declares its slot, as defined in vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md. Hand-authored from docs/design/0010-mandatory-node-values.md, docs/TREE.md and docs/PATH.md as merged in 1a9bb6d, and from nothing else. No implementation of the mandatory API existed when these were written. Items X3, X4 and X20; each note names the defect (W) it catches. 12 cases.

cases.name: m-construct-missing-own-at-root
cases.note: X3. A node without a value is not a node of Node[T]: every existing node carries exactly one opaque T, and the generic core imposes no default value (ADR 0010 §1). Catches W2. Under this slot a conflating adapter, one that reads a missing own as null, also refuses, because null is not a fixture payload. So this case alone cannot tell the right refusal from the wrong one; m-construct-missing-own-under-the-json-slot can.

cases.name: m-construct-missing-own-on-a-child
cases.note: X3. The same at depth one: the child at [61] has no value, so the whole spelling does not construct. Catches W2.

cases.name: m-construct-missing-own-under-the-option-slot
cases.note: X3. The most pointed form of W2. Even when T = Option[fixture], a missing own is not read as none. none must be supplied explicitly (TREE: optionality is a slot choice; ADR 0010 §2: no hidden option around every T). An automatic option wrapper would construct Node(none, ∅) here.

cases.name: m-construct-explicit-none-under-the-option-slot
cases.note: X3, X4. The control for the previous case: none supplied explicitly is a legal payload, so the node constructs.

cases.name: m-construct-explicit-null-under-the-json-slot
cases.note: X4. The control for m-construct-missing-own-under-the-json-slot, in the same slot. An own field holding null supplies a value, and a missing own field supplies none. Both nodes exist. Catches an implementation that rejects null or treats it as absent (W3).

cases.name: m-construct-missing-own-under-the-json-slot
cases.note: X3, X4. The discriminating form of W2. Under the json slot null is a legal payload, so an adapter that reads a missing own field as null (Python dict.get, serde Option<Value>, Go interface{}) would construct Node(null, ∅) and fail here. The spelling has no value, so it must not construct. The pair to m-construct-explicit-null-under-the-json-slot, in the same slot.

cases.name: m-construct-missing-own-on-a-child-under-the-json-slot
cases.note: X3, X4. The same one level down: the child at [61] has no own field, and it is not read as null.

cases.name: m-construct-missing-own-under-the-unit-slot
cases.note: X3. Under Node[Unit] there is exactly one value, and defaulting to it is the tempting convenience. ADR 0010 §1 imposes no default value and makes no exception for the unit, so a missing own does not construct here either.

cases.name: m-construct-duplicate-key-adjacent
cases.note: X20. Keys are unique among siblings (ADR 0010 §3); the same key twice, back to back.

cases.name: m-construct-duplicate-key-nonadjacent
cases.note: X20. A distinct key sits between the two occurrences. A check that compares only neighbours misses it.

cases.name: m-construct-duplicate-empty-key
cases.note: X20, X19. The empty key is a key and occupies its slot exactly once. Under Node[Unit] the two subtrees are equal, and that still does not merge them.

cases.name: m-construct-duplicate-with-equal-children-is-not-merged
cases.note: X20. The two subtrees are ≈ (same class). A construction that drops one of two equal entries instead of refusing fails here: a finite map has no second entry to merge.
